# How Silicon Valley Took Over the Defense Industry with Peter Arment | The Real Eisman Playbook Ep 61

First listed: 2026-05-25 | Evaluation cutoff: 2026-11-10

[Back to library](../README.md)

## Source versions

- [YouTube: How Silicon Valley Took Over the Defense Industry with Peter Arment | The Real Eisman Playbook Ep 61](https://www.youtube.com/watch?v=VElWGgso2FY) - 2026-05-25
- [Substack: How Silicon Valley Took Over the Defense Industry with Peter Arment | The Real Eisman Playbook Ep 61](https://realeismanplaybook.substack.com/p/how-silicon-valley-took-over-the) - 2026-05-25

Earliest listed publication among matched versions, not proof of an unedited contemporaneous archive. Claim timestamps refer to the reviewed version.

## Summary

Peter Arment explains defense consolidation, replenishment demand and the opportunity for cheaper systems and new entrants. He separates durable order books from valuation, discusses Boeing recovery and highlights nuclear suppliers. Eisman favors further research on nimble defense firms, Curtiss-Wright and BWXT. Reported backlog and supplier growth support several premises, while procurement reform, hypothetical breakups and multiyear nuclear projects remain unfinished.

Claims are assessed individually. Empirical premises are not treated as successful forecasts. Unverified magnitudes and causal stories remain unresolved; subjective investment judgments are not assigned directional wins.

## Framework and tools

- Separate spending demand from valuation and execution.
- Compare mission-level effectiveness as well as weapon purchase cost.
- Distinguish aggregate project revenue from annual earnings.
- Follow per-share economics when recapitalizations dilute ownership.
- Treat exploratory research interest separately from timed forecasts.

Tools and charts discussed, not a complete visual inspection:

- Prime-contractor market concentration and procurement shares.
- Budget base versus reconciliation funding.
- Weapon cost and replenishment lead times.
- Lockheed sum-of-parts scenario.
- Boeing production and FCF per share.
- AP1000 plant count times pumps, price and margin.

## Source cautions

Steve Eisman interviews Peter Arment. The closing recap is Eisman; most industry projections are Arment.
- Opening montage duplicates later discussion and is not separately counted.
- Automatically generated captions have company-name errors; no unsupported tickers are inferred.
- A speculative claim about the origins of German environmental politics is not treated as established evidence.
- Guest claims remain attributed to Peter Arment.
